title: Anchored log ingestor with OTLP hook and ordered replay coordinator
creator: Sophie Chen
description: Build a resilient, tenant-aware log ingestion path that anchors incoming structured log envelopes into a lightweight commit ledger and exposes an OTLP-compatible hook for tracing correlation. The new flow must guarantee per-session ordering for replay, support soft-commits for low-latency downstream visibility, and provide a replay coordinator that can deterministically rehydrate missed envelopes into Loki or ELK backends with minimal duplication.
background: Current ingest flows occasionally lose ordering guarantees for multi-event sessions under burst load and lack a standard OTLP hook that ties trace/span IDs to log envelopes before they reach downstream sinks. This causes difficulties for SREs when reconstructing end-to-end traces across the runtime and the console. Several related tickets (see dependencies) prototyped prefix-caching and tenant-aware routing but didn't address ordered replays or an explicit anchoring layer.
technical_design: We will introduce three components: 1) Anchoring service: a lightweight append-only ledger (per-tenant shard) that assigns a monotonic anchor ID and soft-commit flag to each incoming envelope; 2) OTLP Hook Adapter: an inline transform that extracts/normalizes OpenTelemetry trace/span identifiers, injects them into the anchored envelope metadata, and emits a small OTLP event to the tracing pipeline for immediate joins; 3) Ordered Replay Coordinator: a controller that reads the anchor ledger and replays ranges deterministically to downstream connectors (Loki/ELK) with idempotency keys derived from tenant+anchor_id+hash(envelope). The anchoring service stores minimal KV state (last-committed-anchor, pending window) and exposes an HTTP tailing API for low-latency consumers.
ingest_path: edge -> prefilter -> OTLP Hook Adapter -> Anchoring service -> soft-commit -> kafka topic (anchored-envelopes) -> downstream connectors or replay coordinator
acceptance_criteria: 1) All envelopes receive anchor IDs and can be queried by anchor range for a tenant. 2) OTLP Hook emits a trace join event for >=95% of incoming envelopes with trace context. 3) In a synthetic burst test (10k/s for 1 minute), session-ordered sequences are replayed to Loki without reordering in 99.9% of cases. 4) Replay coordinator must not create duplicate visible entries in Loki/ELK when rehydrating already-soft-committed ranges. 5) Metrics for anchor lag, replay success rate, and OTLP join latency are available in Console.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): deploy anchoring service + OTLP Hook Adapter in eu-west-1 for beta tenants behind a feature flag; monitor anchor lag and OTLP join events. Phase 2: enable kafka-backed soft-commit for more tenants and run deterministic replay tests. Phase 3: global rollout with automatic fallback to legacy ingest if anchor store is unavailable. Defer schema migration by supporting both new metadata fields and backward-compatible envelope shape.
migration_and_backcompat: Anchored envelopes add a top-level 'anchor' object. Downstream connectors will ignore unknown fields; legacy consumers will still receive original envelope body. Provide a compatibility shim in the transform layer that can strip anchor metadata for consumers that cannot accept it.
observability_and_metrics: New metrics: anchor.append.latency_ms, anchor.commit.lag, anchor.replay.success_rate, otlp.hook.emit_latency_ms, otlp.hook.missing_trace_pct, replay.duplicate_rate. Dashboards: anchor health, per-tenant lag heatmap, replay throughput and error trends. Alerting: anchor.commit.lag > 5s for >5m (P0), replay.duplicate_rate > 0.1% (P1).
security_and_privacy: Anchoring ledger stores only minimal metadata and a reference to the envelope; payloads remain encrypted-at-rest and tenant-isolated. Ensure KMS encryption keys for the anchor store and enforce RBAC on the tailing API. Security review not required for this iteration, but we'll add HSM/KMS integration in the private deployment path.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: anchoring service becomes hot shard under a large tenant. Mitigation: shard by tenant+session-hash and provide tenant-level rate limiting; implement backpressure to prefilter. Risk: duplicate deliveries during replay. Mitigation: use idempotency keys and downstream dedupe table plus soft-commit markers to avoid exposing replays as new entries.
outstanding_questions: What is the retention window for anchor ledgers per tenant? (default proposal: 7d)
Should the OTLP Hook emit full span payloads or only trace/span IDs to reduce wire overhead?
What's the target RPS per shard for initial capacity planning?
